# NPM Improved v1.3.1 — Rolling NPMX Updates

The native **Settings → Update** manager now supports sequential NPMX Primary/Secondary upgrades, restarts and rollbacks without requiring Instance Synchronization to be disabled.

## Fixes

- Removes the blanket updater refusal when Instance Synchronization is enabled.
- Keeps existing database migration, shared-MySQL, disaster recovery, password, same-node concurrent action, Docker health and rollback safeguards.
- The Update page identifies the NPMX role and explains how to update peers one after another.
- While peer application versions differ, NPMX intentionally refuses configuration snapshots and automatically resumes them when versions match.

## How to upgrade

Update one node, verify its proxy and Control Center health, then update the second node. **Do not start both updates at once.** This is an operator-managed sequential process; it does not add a distributed update lock.

Each node restarts briefly. Transparent availability depends on your own traffic failover arrangement. No simultaneous restart or blanket maintenance window is required.

### Existing installations with the old block

An installed image containing the old updater restriction cannot unlock itself before updating. Perform a **one-time sequential Docker Compose upgrade** to v1.3.1 on each blocked node. Future releases can use Settings → Update.

**Shared MySQL deployments** still block single-node updates; they are not covered by NPMX rolling upgrades.
